claims.text: Coherent nanoprecipitations can provide high mechanical strength in a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
The specific W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloy is a high-strength alloy whose strength is provided by coherent nanoprecipitations.
Refractory high-entropy alloys have excellent mechanical properties at elevated temperatures.
Introducing a lubricious secondary phase into a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy will produce wide-temperature self-lubrication.
Nanoscale tungsten disulfide particles can be introduced into the refractory high-entropy-alloy matrix as a lubricating phase.
Suitable alloying additions can promote formation of a surface oxide film on a refractory high-entropy alloy at high temperature.
The alloying-induced oxide film will be lubricious rather than merely oxidation-protective.
Nanoscale precipitates or in-situ tribolayers at the alloy surface will act as solid lubricants.
At high temperatures, the secondary phase will remain stable or transform into a continuous lubricious film.
The continuous lubricious film will reduce friction and wear.
The coherent-nanoprecipitate matrix will retain structural integrity and high strength at elevated temperature.
The modified alloy will have lower friction and better wear resistance than the unmodified tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy over the target temperature range.
The modified alloy will maintain mechanical strength comparable to the baseline despite addition of the lubricating phase.
The relevant wide-temperature operating range can extend from ambient temperature to approximately 800-1600 °C.
Self-lubrication will depend on atmosphere and on the temperature interval over which the lubricious film remains stable.
